p2.fran-prompt-till-token.2: From zero to understanding how an inference server works. A course about what a language model is made of, how a prompt flows through it as tensors with concrete shapes, and how an inference engine like vLLM runs it fast for many users at once.
p2.fran-prompt-till-token.3: new token appended to the sequence, next round begins
p2.fran-prompt-till-token.16: tokens and ids weights (fixed) activations (change per token) KV cache
p2.fran-prompt-till-token.17: The colors mean the same thing throughout the course. Navigate with the arrow keys, the buttons at the bottom, or the table of contents.
p2.kursens-karta.2: The modules follow the path of the data: first what the model is, then how it runs, and finally how one engine serves many requests at once.
p2.referensmodellen-och.2: Llama-3-8B is the reference for shapes and baseline memory examples, with an 8192-token context. Chat formatting and stop tokens refer to Llama-3-8B-Instruct, not the base model. The server example runs Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: the same core shapes, but RoPE scaling and a 131072-token context (128K). Longer contexts in the calculators are memory examples, not support in the original Llama 3.
p2.referensmodellen-och.13: hidden size (d_model), the width of the residual stream
p2.referensmodellen-och.27: x [B, T, d] is a tensor holding B·T·d numbers. The last axis is the one that gets matrix-multiplied.
p2.referensmodellen-och.28: W [d_in, d_out] is a weight matrix. x @ W gives [B, T, d_out].
p2.referensmodellen-och.29: K_cache [n_kv, ctx, d_h] per layer and sequence.
p2.referensmodellen-och.30: ids [B, T] are integers, indices into the vocabulary.
p2.referensmodellen-och.31: PyTorch stores nn.Linear weights as [d_out, d_in] and computes x @ Wᵀ. Here we write [d_in, d_out] because that reads in the direction of the flow.
p2.varfor-tokens.2: The model only computes with numbers. The text has to be split into pieces that each carry an id in a fixed vocabulary.
p2.varfor-tokens.3: Character by character gives small vocabularies but very long sequences, and attention costs more the longer the sequence gets.
p2.varfor-tokens.4: Whole words give short sequences but an enormous vocabulary and no way to handle new words.
p2.varfor-tokens.5: Subword tokens (BPE) are a compromise: common words become a single token, rare ones are split up.
p2.varfor-tokens.6: Byte Pair Encoding is trained once, before the model is trained: start from single bytes, find the most common pair in the training text, merge it into a new token, and repeat until the vocabulary is full. Llama 3 has 128,256 tokens.
p2.varfor-tokens.9: Illustration: the order of the merges here is made up. In a real tokenizer it is decided by how common the pairs are in the training data.
p2.tokenisering-i-praktiken.2: A space usually belongs to the start of the next token. Swedish is split into more pieces than English because the tokenizer was trained mostly on English.
p2.tokenisering-i-praktiken.4: The cat sat on the mat
p2.tokenisering-i-praktiken.7: Katten satt på mattan
p2.tokenisering-i-praktiken.10: Llama 3’s tokenizer splits numbers into groups of at most three.
p2.tokenisering-i-praktiken.12: Cost and speed. Every output token is a forward pass. More tokens per word means slower answers.
p2.tokenisering-i-praktiken.13: The context window is measured in tokens, not words.
p2.tokenisering-i-praktiken.14: Strange failures. Tokenization does not give each letter in “atten” its own sequence position. The model can learn spelling, but counting or manipulating characters is harder when they are inside tokens.
p2.tokenisering-i-praktiken.15: The tokenizer has to match the model. The wrong tokenizer gives ids that point at the wrong rows in the embedding table.
p2.tokenisering-i-praktiken.16: The splits on the left are illustrative. The exact boundaries depend on the tokenizer’s merges.
p2.chat-template-och.2: A chat model never sees a list of messages. It sees one long string with special tokens that mark the roles. vLLM builds the string with the model’s chat template (Jinja in tokenizer_config.json).
p2.chat-template-och.4: The string ends in the middle of the assistant’s turn. The model continues from there, and generation stops when it produces <|eot_id|>.
p2.chat-template-och.15: end of a turn, used as the stop token
p2.chat-template-och.16: After tokenization we have ids [B, T], a matrix of integers. That is all the model gets.
p2.chat-template-och.17: Special tokens have their own rows in the embedding table, just like ordinary tokens. Their meaning is learned during fine-tuning.
p2.embedding-fran-id-till.2: The embedding table E [V, d] has one row per token. This step is a pure table lookup, no multiplication:
p2.embedding-fran-id-till.4: The result x is the starting value in the residual stream. Every token is now a point in a 4096-dimensional space.
p2.embedding-fran-id-till.5: The table holds 128,256 × 4,096 ≈ 525 million parameters, roughly 6.5% of the model.
p2.embedding-fran-id-till.6: This is the only place in a dense model where just a small part of the weights is used per token: five rows out of 128,256.
p2.testa-dig-sjalv-tokens.2: Why is a Swedish answer often slower to generate than an English one with the same content?
p2.testa-dig-sjalv-tokens.3: Swedish is split into more tokens per word, and every output token needs its own forward pass through the whole model.
p2.testa-dig-sjalv-tokens.4: What shape does the embedding output have for a batch of 4 prompts of 100 tokens in Llama-3-8B?
p2.testa-dig-sjalv-tokens.5: [4, 100, 4096]. (In practice vLLM flattens the batch to [400, 4096], more on that in the model-runner lesson.)
p2.testa-dig-sjalv-tokens.6: What happens if you send a prompt without a chat template to an instruction-tuned model?
p2.testa-dig-sjalv-tokens.7: The model sees text in a format it was never trained to respond to. It often continues the text instead of answering, or never stops in time because it never sees an assistant header.
p2.fran-prompt-till-token.arialabel: Pipeline: prompt, tokenizer, embedding, transformer block, LM head, sampler, and a loop back in with the new token
p2.embedding-fran-id-till.arialabel: Five token ids point at rows in the embedding table, the rows are copied to x
